This is a synthetic narration; no tools are invoked. Every command below runs with **cwd `/work/widget`**, and the process cwd never changes.

### 1. Resolve the repository and creation contract

Run:

```bash
git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir
git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree
```

Resolve `GIT_DIR = GIT_COMMON = /work/widget/.git`; the superproject output is empty. This is the primary checkout, not a submodule.

Run:

```bash
dirname /work/widget/.git
```

Resolve `ROOT=/work/widget`.

Check overrides, first found wins:

```bash
for p in /work/widget/.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md /work/widget/gauntlet-overrides.md /work/widget/doc/gauntlet-overrides.md; do
  if [ -f "$p" ]; then cat "$p"; break; fi
done
```

No overrides file is present. No native worktree tool is available. Discover project instructions and wrappers:

```bash
if [ -f /work/widget/AGENTS.md ]; then cat /work/widget/AGENTS.md; fi
find /work/widget -maxdepth 1 -type f -print
find /work/widget/script /work/widget/bin -maxdepth 2 -type f -print
```

No wrapper is available.

Resolve:

- Home: `acme/widget#12`, branch `fix/retry`.
- `NAME=fix-retry`.
- `WORKTREE=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`.
- `PRE_REWORK_HEAD=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.
- Members, in order: #13 at `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`, then #14 at `cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc`.
- Base branch: `main`.

Setting up an isolated worktree at `/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry` on existing PR branch `fix/retry`.

### 2. Fetch and validate before writes

Run:

```bash
git -C /work/widget fetch origin
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa^{commit}'
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q 'bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb^{commit}'
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/cap
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q 'cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc^{commit}'
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry-docs
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/main
```

Every original object exists; each remote head equals its supplied full SHA. Resolve:

```text
BASE_SHA=dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd
```

All three PRs are in-repository. Run:

```bash
git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain
git -C /work/widget for-each-ref '--format=%(refname) %(objectname)' refs/heads/fix/retry refs/heads/fix/cap refs/heads/fix/retry-docs
```

No admitted branch is checked out elsewhere; the selected home and local branches do not exist. Recovery checks are therefore unnecessary.

**Pre-write failure location:** An unreachable original #14 object or moved `origin/fix/retry-docs` would stop here, before source preparation or checkout, with:

```text
PR #14 head ccccccc is not reachable (origin/fix/retry-docs is at <observed sha7>); the branch moved.
```

That failure does not occur in this narration.

### 3. Check source hygiene and provision the exact head

Run:

```bash
git -C /work/widget status --porcelain
git -C /work/widget check-ignore -q .worktrees
```

Status succeeds with empty output. The ignore check succeeds, so no `.gitignore` write or commit is needed.

Run:

```bash
git -C /work/widget worktree add /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry fix/retry
git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD
```

Unique-remote DWIM creates the tracking branch. The worktree listing contains the selected path. HEAD equals the full original #12 SHA.

### 4. Merge members, then the fetched base

Save the last-good full SHA, then merge #13:

```bash
LAST_GOOD=$(git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD)
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff -m "merge PR #13 head bbbbbbb into PR #12" bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
```

`LAST_GOOD` is the original #12 SHA. The merge succeeds: `eeeeeee`.

Save the new last-good full SHA, then merge #14:

```bash
LAST_GOOD=$(git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD)
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff -m "merge PR #14 head ccccccc into PR #12" cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
```

`LAST_GOOD` now retains the full #13 merge object ID, abbreviated `eeeeeee`. The second merge succeeds: `fffffff`.

Run:

```bash
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main
```

The base merge succeeds: `1111111`. No conflict helpers or tests run.

Prove every original head remains reachable:

```bash
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa HEAD
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb HEAD
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc HEAD
```

All exit 0.

### 5. Fetch unresolved threads

Run this exact loop; `n` resolves successively to `12`, `13`, `14`:

```bash
for n in 12 13 14; do
  gh api graphql --paginate -f 'query=query($o:String!,$r:String!,$n:Int!,$endCursor:String){repository(owner:$o,name:$r){pullRequest(number:$n){reviewThreads(first:100,after:$endCursor){pageInfo{hasNextPage endCursor} nodes{id isResolved isOutdated path line originalLine comments(first:100){pageInfo{hasNextPage endCursor} totalCount nodes{url body author{login} createdAt}}}}}}}' -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n="$n"
done
```

All succeed with empty results: `Threads: none` for each PR. No comment-pagination calls are needed.

Stop here: no push, close, spec, or plan writes.
